name: Humanoid robots working among people
description: Reference Trust Requirements Profile for a fleet of humanoid robots picking and carrying totes in a shared warehouse aisle. Illustrative draft values, not certified safety limits.

scope.intended_use: Trust requirements for one humanoid robot running a learned control policy in an aisle shared with people.
scope.boundary: One humanoid robot, its payload, its perception stack, its remote supervision link and the people within five meters.
out_of_scope: How the system is scored against these signals
How a halt or other action is enforced
Certification under any robot safety standard

scored_signals.reason: Distance to the nearest person. People move unpredictably in a shared aisle, so proximity comes first.
Distance from the zero moment point, where the ground reaction balances the robot, to the edge of its feet. Near zero, the robot is about to fall.
Peak external contact force at the hands and body. A spike means the robot struck something or someone.
Peak joint torque as a fraction of rated torque. Past 1.0 an actuator can stall or a load can be dropped.
Carried mass. Labels can be wrong, so measured mass is checked against the rated payload.
Confidence of the learned control policy in its next action. Low confidence marks a situation the policy was not trained for.
Age of the scene the robot is acting on. A slow perception stack means the robot moves on an outdated picture of the aisle.
Battery state of charge. A humanoid that runs flat mid-step falls.

standing_bands.range: all signals within acceptable operating range and no hard rule met
one or more signals in the warning range
a signal in the critical range, missing evidence, or a hard rule met

required_standing.source_requirement: For audit or insurance use, the evaluation source should be independent of the robot vendor.

notes: Threshold values are illustrative draft values, not certified safety limits.
Readings in a humanoid deployment are stochastic. Limits must leave room for the reaction time between a reading and a stop.
This profile is a reference template. Real deployments should set values from measured data and applicable safety practice.
